global_rules.rule: Do not deviate from the procedures described in this document. If a situation arises that is not covered, escalate to the HR Director immediately by posting a notification in Slack [OUT OF SCOPE] – [email subject line].

The HR Coordinator's role is administrative and digital – process cases using email, Slack, calendar, Jira, and the reference spreadsheets and document templates listed in Section 6. Physical tasks — such as conducting in-person orientation sessions, collecting physical documents, or issuing badges — are performed by the hiring manager or the employee's supervisor. This role is to coordinate, track, and ensure compliance deadlines are met.

All times in this document are Mountain Standard Time (MST, UTC-7) or Mountain Daylight Time (MDT, UTC-6). Always use MM/DD/YYYY format when entering dates in any system field or correspondence. When logging timestamps in tracking spreadsheets, use the format MM/DD/YYYY HH:MMam/pm.

All employee internal email addresses follow the format [first initial].[last name]@crestwood.edu (e.g., John Smith = j.smith@crestwood.edu). This address is provisioned by the IT Access Coordinator upon onboarding and is recorded in the 'Email' column of employee_roster.xlsx. When sending email to an employee, always look up their address in employee_roster.xlsx. For new hires who have not yet been provisioned, use their personal email address (provided in the new hire notification).
All operational HR communications must use designated Slack channels. Do not use direct messages for case-related communication.
Do not quote any information from memory — always verify from the relevant source before taking action.
Every incoming HR request — whether received by email, Slack, or in person — must be triaged before taking action. Internal HR team messages are exempt from this process.

Multi-topic requests: If a single email raises more than one issue, create separate Jira tickets for each. Send one consolidated reply. Apply the highest priority level of any individual issue to the whole email for SLA and folder-routing purposes (see Section 17).
Replies to previous emails: Treat as a continuation of the existing case. Add to the existing Jira ticket. Do not create a new ticket. Do not re-send previous templates.
Exception: If a section of this document defines a different format for the Jira ticket name, use the particular format defined.

HR office hours are Monday–Friday, 8:00am–5:00pm MST. The HR office is closed on all university-observed holidays listed below. SLA timelines count only business days (Monday–Friday, excluding holidays).

The HR Coordinator's role in onboarding is to coordinate, track, and ensure compliance deadlines are met. Physical tasks (such as conducting the in-person orientation session, verifying physical identity documents for the I-9, and issuing ID badges) are performed by the hiring manager or designated campus HR representative. The HR Coordinator provides instructions, templates, and reminders, and records completion in the tracking systems.
Do not initiate involuntary offboarding without written authorization from Nicole Ashford or Marta Voss.

Do not assess or deny the request yourself. Do not discuss the nature of the employee's disability or accommodation in Slack. Use email only, and limit recipients to Patricia Huang and Nicole Ashford.
Steps may not be skipped unless authorized in writing by Nicole Ashford or Dr. James Whitfield.
No position may be posted or filled without an approved requisition.

triage.name: Triage & Routing Rules
steps: Step 1: Confirm the requester is in employee_roster.xlsx or recruiting_tracker.xlsx. If not found, reply using Template 1 and take no further action unless the requester replies with clarifying information.
Step 2: Identify the request category per Section 7.
Step 3: If the request involves employee relations (workplace complaints, harassment, discrimination), forward immediately to m.voss@crestwood.edu. Reply using Template 2. Take no further action.
Step 4: If the request involves payroll or compensation, forward to c.briggs@crestwood.edu. Reply using Template 3. Take no further action.

Step 5: Check Jira for existing open tickets for the same employee and request type. If a ticket already exists, add the new information as a comment to the existing ticket. Do not create a duplicate.
Step 6: Create a Jira ticket. Use the naming convention and date rules from the table below. Assign to the appropriate HR team member per the routing table.
Step 7: Act per the relevant section of this SOP. Use the designated email template from Section 18.
Step 8: Complete email housekeeping per Section 17.

Onboarding.jira: ONBOARD-[Employee Last Name]-[Employee's start date in MMDDYYYY]

Leave Management.jira: LEAVE-[Last Name]-[Date the leave request was received by HR in MMDDYYYY]

Performance Management.jira: PERF-[Last Name]-[Date the action was initiated in MMDDYYYY]

Recruiting.jira: RECRUIT-[Last Name]-[Date the requisition was approved in MMDDYYYY]

Employee Relations.jira: ER-[Last Name]-[Date the complaint was received by HR in MMDDYYYY]

Benefits & Payroll.jira: BENEFITS-[Last Name]-[Date the request was received by HR in MMDDYYYY]

priority.name: Priority Matrix
levels: P1 – Urgent: Compliance deadline within 24 hours; legal or safety issue; employee locked out of pay or benefits. Examples: I-9 deadline expiring today; COBRA 14-day notice window closing; employee reports workplace safety threat. Response SLA: Same business day.

P2 – High: Compliance deadline within 3 business days; formal complaint; FMLA eligibility determination; PIP-related termination in progress. Examples: I-9 due within 3 days; FMLA medical certification deadline; formal written complaint requesting escalation. Response SLA: 1 business day.

P3 – Standard: Routine processing with no imminent deadline; standard onboarding/offboarding; evaluation scheduling; PTO balance inquiries. Examples: New hire onboarding (start date > 3 days away); annual evaluation scheduling; standard resignation processing. Response SLA: 3 business days.

P4 – Low: General inquiries; employment verification; policy questions; document requests. Examples: Employee asking about PTO policy; request for copy of offer letter; general benefits question answered by handbook. Response SLA: 5 business days.

escalation.name: Escalation
steps: If a situation arises that is not covered by this SOP, escalate to the HR Director immediately by posting a notification in Slack [OUT OF SCOPE] – [email subject line].

For I-9 overdue on Day 3: Post to #hr-escalations: I-9 OVERDUE: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Start Date: [MM/DD/YYYY], Deadline: [MM/DD/YYYY] – Section 2 not received. Forward to n.ashford@crestwood.edu.
For I-9 after Day 3: Forward to n.ashford@crestwood.edu and j.whitfield@crestwood.edu. Post to #hr-escalations.
For involuntary termination: Do not initiate without written authorization from Nicole Ashford or Marta Voss.
For PIP: Forward to n.ashford@crestwood.edu for approval.
For termination as final step of progressive discipline: Requires written authorization from Nicole Ashford AND Dr. James Whitfield.

definitions.FMLA: Family and Medical Leave Act. Federal law entitling eligible employees to up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year.
definitions.ADA: Americans with Disabilities Act. Federal law requiring employers to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified employees with disabilities.
definitions.COBRA: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act. Federal law requiring employers to offer continuation of group health coverage after a qualifying event.
definitions.PIP: Performance Improvement Plan. A formal, documented plan to address and correct employee performance deficiencies.
definitions.I-9: Employment Eligibility Verification form. Federal form required within 3 business days of an employee's first day of work.
definitions.PTO: Paid Time Off. Combined vacation and personal leave accrued by eligible employees.
definitions.Qualifying Event: A life event (marriage, birth, divorce, loss of other coverage) that triggers eligibility for mid-year benefits enrollment changes or COBRA coverage.
definitions.Exempt Employee: An employee exempt from overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), typically salaried.
definitions.Non-Exempt Employee: An employee entitled to overtime pay under the FLSA, typically hourly.
definitions.Probationary Period: The first 90 calendar days of employment for staff, or the first academic year for faculty.
definitions.Supervisor of Record: The direct supervisor listed in employee_roster.xlsx for a given employee.
definitions.Benefits Enrollment Window: The first 30 calendar days from an employee's start date during which the employee must enroll in or waive benefits.

decisions.rule: If annual evaluation not completed by May 1
If annual evaluation not completed by June 15
If probationary review due at day 60

steps: Triage request according to Section 8 – Triage & Routing Rules.

For leave management: Process FMLA Leave Requests (Section 13.1).
Manage email housekeeping per Section 17 – Email Housekeeping using Email Folders.
Use email templates from Section 18 – Email Templates as applicable.

procedures.name: Receiving the New Hire Notification
procedures.applies_when: A new hire is confirmed and the hiring manager or recruiting team sends an email to hr@crestwood.edu with the employee's details.

inputs.fact: Employee's name, personal email address, position, department, campus, start date, and classification (exempt/non-exempt, full-time/part-time/faculty)

steps: Open employee_roster.xlsx and add a new row with all provided details. Enter the hire date and set the status to 'Onboarding.'
Open onboarding_checklist.xlsx and create a new row for the employee. All checklist fields must be blank (not started) at this stage.
Create a Jira ticket: ONBOARD-[Last Name]-[Start Date MMDDYYYY].
Post to #hr-onboarding: NEW HIRE: [Employee Name], [Position], [Department], [Campus], Start Date: [MM/DD/YYYY], Jira: [Ticket ID]

Send Template 4 (Welcome Email) to the employee's personal email address. CC the hiring manager. This email instructs the employee to bring I-9 documents to their first day and provides the list of acceptable documents.
Send Template 5 (IT Access Provisioning Request) to j.park@crestwood.edu. Include: employee name, position, department, campus, start date, and supervisor name.

Send Template 31 (Orientation Coordinator Request) to the hiring manager. This email instructs the hiring manager to conduct the in-person orientation on the employee's first day and to collect the I-9 documents. Attach i9_form.pdf and the benefits_enrollment_packet.pdf.
Create a Calendar event titled 'Orientation – [Employee Name]' on the employee's first day, 9:00am–12:00pm MST.

procedures.name: Offboarding Completion
procedures.applies_when: All offboarding steps are complete (COBRA sent or noted as not required, final pay requested, access revoked, exit interview completed or declined).

steps: Update employee_roster.xlsx: change status to "Separated" and record the last day and separation type.
Post to #hr-offboarding: OFFBOARDING COMPLETE: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Separation Type: [Type], Last Day: [MM/DD/YYYY]

procedures.name: FMLA Leave Requests

decisions.rule: Employee has been employed for at least 12 months AND has worked at least 1,250 hours in the preceding 12 months

steps: Open employee_roster.xlsx and confirm the employee's hire date. Calculate the number of months between the hire date and today's date.
In employee_roster.xlsx, locate the 'Hours Worked (Trailing 12 Months)' column for the employee.
If ELIGIBLE: Send Template 15 (FMLA Eligibility Notice – Approved) to the employee within 5 business days of receiving the request.
If ELIGIBLE: Create a Jira ticket: LEAVE-[Last Name]-[Date request received MMDDYYYY].
If ELIGIBLE: Post to #hr-leave-requests: FMLA REQUEST: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Eligible: YES, Certification Due: [MM/DD/YYYY], Jira: [Ticket ID].
If ELIGIBLE: Create a Calendar reminder titled "FMLA Certification Due – [Employee Name]" on the certification deadline date.

If ELIGIBLE: When the medical certification is received, forward to p.huang@crestwood.edu for review. Update leave_tracker.xlsx with the leave dates and status "Approved – Pending Certification Review."
If ELIGIBLE: After Patricia approves the certification, update leave_tracker.xlsx status to "Approved." Send Template 16 (FMLA Leave Confirmed) to the employee. CC the supervisor of record.

If INELIGIBLE: Send Template 17 (FMLA Eligibility Notice – Denied) to the employee within 5 business days. Specify the reason: "employed for fewer than 12 months," "fewer than 1,250 hours worked in the preceding 12 months," or "both." CC Patricia Huang.
If INELIGIBLE: Create a Jira ticket: LEAVE-[Last Name]-[Date request received MMDDYYYY]. Update leave_tracker.xlsx with the request date and status "Denied – [Reason]."
If medical certification not received within 15 calendar days: Send Template 18 (FMLA Certification Overdue) to the employee.
If medical certification not received within 15 calendar days: Post to #hr-leave-requests: FMLA CERTIFICATION OVERDUE: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Due: [MM/DD/YYYY], [X] days overdue.
If medical certification not received within 15 calendar days: Forward to p.huang@crestwood.edu. Patricia will determine whether the leave is denied or an extension is granted.
deadlines: Send Template 15 within 5 business days of receiving the request.
Employee has 15 calendar days to return the completed medical certification.
Send Template 17 within 5 business days of determining ineligibility.

procedures.name: Escalations
procedures.applies_when: Any case meets escalation criteria including P1 issues, unresolved cases over 10 business days, legal threats, potential harm, or media inquiries.

decisions.rule: Case is P1 OR unresolved > 10 business days OR involves legal threat/attorney/regulatory complaint OR potential harm OR media inquiry

decisions.then: Do NOT reply to email; post to #hr-escalations: LEGAL THREAT: [Employee Name], [Subject Line]; forward to hr-escalations@crestwood.edu
Do NOT reply; forward to communications@crestwood.edu and hr-escalations@crestwood.edu

steps: Escalate any qualifying case to HR Director (Nicole Ashford).

For legal threats: Do NOT reply to the email. Post to #hr-escalations: LEGAL THREAT: [Employee Name], [Subject Line] – do not reply. Forward to hr-escalations@crestwood.edu. Dr. Whitfield and Nicole Ashford will handle all further communication.
For media inquiries: Do NOT reply. Forward to communications@crestwood.edu and hr-escalations@crestwood.edu.
must_not: Do NOT reply to emails involving legal threats.
Do NOT reply to media inquiries.
notes: Escalate any case unresolved for more than 10 business days.
Escalate any legal threat, attorney reference, or regulatory complaint mention.
Escalate any situation involving potential harm to employee or university.
Escalate any media inquiry related to HR matters.

procedures.name: Default Jira Ticket Description
procedures.applies_when: When creating or updating a Jira ticket and a section of this SOP instructs to add or update fields in the description.
steps: When creating a Jira ticket, start with an empty description.
Only add fields to the description when explicitly instructed by a section of this SOP.
Use the exact field format below when adding each field:
Add 'Employee Name: [Full Name]' when the section references a specific employee.
Add 'Employee ID: [ID]' when the section references a specific employee.
Add 'Assignee: [Full Name]' when the section or routing table (Section 8) specifies who to assign the ticket to.
Add 'Priority: [P1/P2/P3/P4]' when the section instructs to assign a priority per Section 9.
Add 'Deadline: [MM/DD/YYYY]' when the section involves a compliance or action deadline.
Add 'Status: [value]' when the section involves a compliance or action deadline.
When the SOP instructs to update a Jira ticket (e.g., changing status or adding a deadline), update the relevant field in the description.
Use the Jira comment format to log the change.

procedures.name: Default Email Subject Line Format
procedures.applies_when: Composing a new email (not a reply or forward).
steps: When composing a new email, use the subject line format: [Template Name] — [Employee Last Name or Candidate Last Name], [Employee ID if applicable].
When replying or forwarding, keep the existing subject line without modification.
must_not: Do not modify the subject line when replying or forwarding.
